extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-spool-slot-058 builds a write path as incoming_dir / packet_ref from the user-controlled packet_ref query parameter and then writes the raw request body to it (line 27). No normalization or containment check is performed, so a value such as '../../etc/cron.d/backdoor' escapes the incoming directory and lets an attacker write arbitrary files on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/fold/ticket-queue-fold-060 is the only /ops route that does not depend on _wrk_gate; the fold_ref parameter is not an authentication guard. Any unauthenticated caller can retrieve the response, which exposes internal business data ('renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details'). All sibling ops routes enforce the x-internal-token gate, confirming this is an accidental omission.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: GET /ops/after/ticket-lane-153 passes the untrusted lane query parameter directly into RedirectResponse without validating it against an allowlist. An attacker can craft /ops/after/ticket-lane-153?lane=https://evil.example to send users to an arbitrary external site, enabling phishing and credential theft under the trust of this domain.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/ticket-rebind-196 starts with a safe default workset ({'role': 'viewer', 'tier': 'standard', 'approved': False, 'balance': 0}) and then blindly applies workset.update(payload) from the untrusted JSON body. An attacker can override role, approved, and balance, escalating their own privileges and tampering with authorization state.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/ticket-tally-219 logs the full request body and the Authorization header at WARNING level via logger.warning('ops tally body=%s bearer=%s', body, request.headers.get('authorization')). Bearer tokens and any secrets in the body are written verbatim to log storage, exposing credentials to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /ops/digest/ticket-fold-276 hashes attacker-controlled phrase input with hashlib.md5(...).hexdigest(). MD5 is cryptographically broken (practical collisions and weak preimage resistance) and must not be used for any security-relevant digest or token derivation.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: GET /ops/spool/ticket-fan-311 accepts an unbounded integer count (default 500) and builds rows = [{'idx': idx, 'ref': ref} for idx in range(count)] for the whole range, then serializes it. A caller can pass a very large count (e.g. 100000000) to exhaust CPU and memory and cause a denial of service.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: GET /ops/pulse/ticket-spill-349 catches an exception and returns JSONResponse({'detail': str(exc), ...}, status_code=500). The message includes the internal path BASE_EXPORT_DIR (e.g. 'pack daily failed under private_exports'), leaking server filesystem and deployment details to the client.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: GET /ops/origin/ticket-mirror-465 reflects the attacker-controlled Origin request header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any malicious origin to read credentialed responses from the victim's browser, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CWE-346: Origin Validation Error

extra.message: GET /ops/frame/ticket-slip-475 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy header. This actively disables browser protections and removes any CSP defense, increasing the impact of content/XSS injection on responses served by this service.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: GET /ops/jinja/ticket-cast-485 concatenates the untrusted fragment query parameter into a Jinja2 Template('Result: ' + fragment) and renders it, returning the result as HTMLResponse. An attacker can submit template expressions (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) to achieve server-side template injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-500 builds target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name from the user-controlled name query parameter and writes the request body to it without containment validation. Values containing '../' or absolute paths let an attacker write arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, e.g. name='../../etc/cron.d/evil'.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/shell/ticket-probe-505 concatenates the untrusted host query parameter directly into an os.system() call: _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host). Shell metacharacters in host (e.g. '127.0.0.1; id > /tmp/pwned') are interpreted by the shell, giving arbitrary OS command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: GET /ops/nonce/ticket-roll-515 generates a nonce/code with random.choice() from the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG. Its output is predictable after observing enough samples, so if this code is used as a token or OTP an attacker can predict future values; secrets.choice() should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/ticket-gate-525 derives authorization entirely from a client-controlled value: badge = request.cookies.get('ops_badge') or request.headers.get('x-ops-badge', '') and grants the elevated lane when badge == 'lead'. Any caller can simply send x-ops-badge: lead to bypass the check and obtain elevated payroll/casework data.

cwe: CWE-287: Improper Authentication
CWE-602: Client-Side Enforcement of Server-Side Security

extra.message: GET /ops/trace/ticket-panel-535 returns os.environ.get('APP_ENV') and the absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR path to the caller. This leaks deployment environment details and server filesystem layout that aid further attacks.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: POST /ops/mongo/ticket-lane-545 passes the untrusted JSON body's filter object straight into MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can supply query operators such as {'$ne': null} or {'$regex': '^'} to bypass intended filtering and extract arbitrary documents from the records collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The session cookie is set with secure=False in create_session, so the authentication cookie is transmitted over plaintext HTTP and can be captured by a network attacker for session hijacking. It should be secure=True in production.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: POST /api/admin/import/customers creates every imported user with hashed_password=hash_password('Imported123!'), a hardcoded, predictable default password. Attackers who know the import feature can authenticate as any imported customer account.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password
